records.label: spacr.train_compare#11
records.source: **k-fold runs keep their folds.** ``folds='per_fold'`` (the default) draws every fold; ``folds='mean'`` draws the fold mean with a ±1 sd band and labels it ``mean of k folds ±sd``; ``folds='both'`` draws both. A mean curve rendered as if it were a single run hides precisely the fold-to-fold variance k-fold was added to expose — and because folds can stop at different epochs (early stopping), the mean carries an ``n_folds`` column so a tail computed from two of five folds is visible rather than implied.
records.context: **k-fold runs keep their folds.** ``folds='per_fold'`` (the default) draws every fold; ``folds='mean'`` draws the fold mean with a ±1 sd band and labels it ``mean of k folds ±sd``; ``folds='both'`` draws both. A mean curve rendered as if it were a single run hides precisely the fold-to-fold variance k-fold was added to expose — and because folds can stop at different epochs (early stopping), the mean carries an ``n_folds`` column so a tail computed from two of five folds is visible rather than implied.
records.translation: **K-falda keyrslur halda faldunum sínum.** ``folds='per_fold'`` (sjálfgefið) teiknar alla faldas; ``folds='mean'`` teiknar meðalfalda með ±1 staðalfrávik bandi og merkir það ``mean of k folds ±sd``; ``folds='both'`` teiknar bæði. Meðal-lúna sem sýnd er eins og hún væri ein keyrsla leynir nákvæmlega þeim breytileika milli falda sem k-falda var bætt við til að sýna — og vegna þess að faldar geta hætt á mismunandi tímamótum (snemmhætting), inniheldur meðal-tálinn ``n_folds`` dálk svo aftantesla reiknuð úr tveimur af fimm földum sjáist frekar en aðeins gefist í skyn.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.agreement#1
records.source: The Annotate app writes one ``INTEGER`` column per pass into ``png_list``. Two people labelling the same crops therefore leave two columns side by side, and the only question that matters before either set is used as ground truth is: *do they agree, and where don't they?*
records.context: The Annotate app writes one ``INTEGER`` column per pass into ``png_list``. Two people labelling the same extracted image regions therefore leave two columns side by side, and the only question that matters before either set is used as ground truth is: *do they agree, and where don't they?*
records.translation: Forritið Annotate skrifar eina ``INTEGER`` dálk á hverja umferð í ``png_list``. Því skilja tveir einstaklingar sem merkja sömu útdrættu myndasvæðin eftir tvo dálka hlið við hlið, og eina spurningin sem skiptir máli áður en annað settið er notað sem raunverulegur sannleikur er: *eru þeir sammála, og hvar gera þau það ekki?*

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dose_response.candidate_concentration_columns#2
records.source: Note what is *not* required: :data:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec. CONTINUOUS`. The shared classifier calls a low-cardinality numeric column categorical, which is the right call for ``cell_count`` and the wrong one here — an eight-point dilution series has exactly eight levels *by design*, so the classifier's own rule would hide every concentration column in the project. The classifier is still what excludes object keys and free text (:data:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.UNPLOTTABLE`), which is the part of its judgement that transfers; the continuous/categorical split is simply not the cut a dose column falls on.
records.context: Note what is *not* required: :data:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec. CONTINUOUS`. The shared machine-learning classification model calls a low-cardinality numeric column categorical, which is the right call for ``cell_count`` and the wrong one here — an eight-point dilution series has exactly eight levels *by design*, so the machine-learning classification model's own rule would hide every concentration column in the project. The machine-learning classification model is still what excludes object identifiers and free text (:data:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.UNPLOTTABLE`), which is the part of its judgement that transfers; the continuous/categorical split is simply not the cut a dose column falls on.
records.translation: Taktu eftir því hvað er *ekki* krafist: :data:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec. CONTINUOUS`. Sameiginlegi vélanámstýpuflokkunarlíkanið kallar lággildi tölugrein flokkun, sem er rétt ákvörðun fyrir ``cell_count`` og röng hér — átta þynningarröð hefur nákvæmlega átta stig *eftir hönnun*, þannig að reglan sjálf hjá vélanámstýpuflokkunarlíkaninu myndi fela allar styrkleikagreinarnar í verkefninu. Vélanámstýpuflokkunarlíkaninu er enn um það bil að útiloka hlutagrunnanatæki og frjálsa texta (:data:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.UNPLOTTABLE`), sem er sú ákvörðun þess sem flyst; skiptingin í samfellda/flokkaða er einfaldlega ekki sú sem skammtaröðin lendir á.

records.label: spacr.hits.load_gene_metadata#1
records.source: A curated export lists a gene once per transcript. The bundled ``toxoplasma_metadata.csv`` repeats 30 Gene IDs between 2 and 32 times, each copy carrying a different protein length and GO-term set. Joined as-is, every one of those genes multiplies in the results — which is a hit list that counts the same gene as up to 32 independent findings.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.outliers#7
records.source: The **Objects** tab is the per-object flags; the **Wells** tab is the across-well pass. They are separate tabs rather than one merged view because they answer different questions and routinely disagree: a well shifted as a whole flags almost none of its individual objects and is nevertheless the loudest point among wells. The engine's ``report()`` is shown verbatim in the third tab, caveats included — the share flagged is not interpretable without the sentence saying whether a symmetric fence on skewed data produced it.
records.context: The **Objects** tab is the per-object flags; the **Microplate sample positions** tab is the across-well pass. They are separate tabs rather than one merged view because they answer different questions and routinely disagree: a well shifted as a whole flags almost none of its individual objects and is nevertheless the loudest point among microplate sample positions. The engine's ``report()`` is shown verbatim in the third tab, caveats included — the share flagged is not interpretable without the sentence saying whether a symmetric fence on skewed data produced it.
records.translation: Flipa **Objects** sýnir fánana fyrir hvert hlut; flipa **Microplate sample positions** sýnir flæði yfir öll holin. Þær eru aðskildar flipar í stað þess að vera sameinaður útsýni því þær svara mismunandi spurningum og eru gjarnan ósammála: hola sem hvolfað er sem heild flaggar næstum engum einstaklingshlutum sínum en er engu að síður háværasti punkturinn meðal sýninga á microplate-stökum hlutum. Vélin ``report()`` er sýnd orðrétt á þriðja flipanum, með fyrirvara — hver hluti flaggaður er túlkunarlaus án setningar sem segir hvort samhverfur girðing á skakkaðri gögn hafi framkallað það.

records.context: **The fit runs off the main GUI execution path** through :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`, like every other read and compute in the Qt layer. A profile-likelihood interval on a 96-compound laboratory microplate is seconds, not milliseconds, and ``threaded=False`` runs the identical code inline so a test drives the same path the shipped application view does.

Þekju-líkinda bilið á 96-sambandshátt smáskiefu í tilraunastofu er sekúndur, ekki millisekúndur, og ``threaded=False`` keyrir nákvæmlega sama kóða innlínulega þannig að próf keyrir sömu leið og sýnilega forritið sem sent var út gerir.

records.label: spacr.qt.bridge.prune_job_pairs#2
records.source: The slot is queued onto the GUI thread, so it runs *after* the OS thread has gone. ``make_thread`` also wires ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater``, and the same pump that delivers this call flushes that deferred delete first — so ``isRunning()`` raises ``RuntimeError: Internal C++ object already deleted`` from inside a Qt slot. The list comprehension never completes and **every** pair is retained, forever, along with its worker.
records.context: The slot is queued onto the main GUI execution path, so it executes *after* the OS independent execution path has gone. ``make_thread`` also wires ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater``, and the same pump that delivers this call flushes that deferred delete first — so ``isRunning()`` raises ``RuntimeError: Internal C++ object already deleted`` from inside a Qt slot. The list comprehension never completes and **every** pair is retained, forever, along with its worker.
records.translation: Raufin er raðað inn á aðal GUI framkvæmdarleið, svo hún framkvæmist *eftir* að stýrikerfisóháða framkvæmdarleiðin hefur farið. ``make_thread`` tengir einnig ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater``, og sama dælan sem sendir þetta kall hreinsar þá sjálfgefið brottfar fyrst — svo ``isRunning()`` kallar á ``RuntimeError: Internal C++ object already deleted`` innan Qt raftar. Listasamsetningin lýkur aldrei og **hverjum** pörum er haldið, að eilífu, ásamt vinnumanni sínum.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.dose_response.register#3
records.source: ``SECTION_DESIGN``, which is not the obvious answer and is the right one. Design is "everything that happens before the microscope: power, sample size, plate layout, controls and replicates", and it already holds Power / Design. A dose–response series is the *other* pre-experiment calculation a screening lab runs: nobody fits an EC50 to admire it, they fit it to pick the concentration the actual screen will use, exactly as they run a power calculation to pick n. The output of this screen is an input to the next experiment, which is what the section means.
records.context: ``SECTION_DESIGN``, which is not the obvious answer and is the right one. Design is "everything that happens before the microscope: statistical detection sensitivity, sample size, laboratory microplate layout, controls and replicates", and it already holds statistical detection sensitivity / Design. A dose–response series is the *other* pre-experiment calculation a screening lab runs: nobody fits an EC50 to admire it, they fit it to pick the concentration the actual screen will use, exactly as they run a statistical detection sensitivity calculation to pick n. The output of this screen is an input to the next experiment, which is what the section means.
records.translation: ``SECTION_DESIGN``, sem er ekki augljós svar en er rétt svar. Hönnun er „allt sem gerist áður en smásjáran kemur: tölfræðileg uppgötvunarviðkvæmni, sýnisstærð, uppsetning á rannsóknarstofulínum, stjórn- og endurtekningarsýni“, og hún inniheldur þegar tölfræðilega uppgötvunarviðkvæmni / hönnun. Skammt–svar röð er *önnur* for-tilraun útreikningur sem skimunarstofan keyrir: enginn passar EC50 til að dáast að henni, þeir passa hana til að velja styrkinn sem raunverulega skimunin mun nota, nákvæmlega eins og þeir framkvæma tölfræðilega uppgötvunarviðkvæmnisútreikning til að velja n. Úttak þessarar skimunar er inntak í næstu tilraun, sem er það sem kaflinn á við.

records.label: spacr.layers#1
records.source: Every viewer spaCR has ever shipped draws one thing. The live preview draws an image with outlines burnt into it; the timelapse preview draws a frame with tracks burnt into it; Make Masks draws an image with a brush burnt into it. "Burnt in" is the problem: the mask is not a *thing* you can hide, fade, recolour or put underneath something else — it is pixels that were already RGB by the time the widget saw them.
records.context: Every viewer spaCR has ever shipped draws one thing. The live preview draws an image with outlines burnt into it; the timelapse preview draws a frame with tracks burnt into it; Make Masks draws an image with a brush burnt into it. "Burnt in" is the problem: the mask is not a *thing* you can hide, fade, recolour or put underneath something else — it is pixels that were already RGB by the time the widget saw them.
records.translation: Allur áhorfandi spaCR hefur nokkurn tíma sent teiknar eitt hlut. Rauntíma forskoðunin teiknar mynd með útlínum brenndum inn í hana; tímaröðaforskoðunin teiknar ramma með sporum brenndum inn í hana; Gerðu grímur teiknar mynd með burstabaug brenndum inn í hana. "Burnt in" er vandamálið: gríman er ekki *hlutur* sem þú getur falið, dofnað, endurlitað eða lagt undir eitthvað annað — hún er pixlar sem voru þegar RGB þegar viðmótið sá þau.

records.label: spacr.crops.crop_spec_from_settings#2
records.source: the ``measure_crop`` settings. The per-``crop_mode`` lists (``png_size``, ``dialate_pngs``, ``dialate_png_ratios``) are indexed by where the chosen object type sits in ``crop_mode``, and fall back to entry 0 when it is not listed there. The crop's channels come from ``png_channel_mapping`` -- or the legacy ``png_dims`` -- via :func:`channels_from_settings`, so the spec is in colour order, not ``png_dims`` list order. A ``normalize`` that is a sequence of any length but 2 is discarded as ``False``.
records.context: the ``measure_crop`` settings. The per-``crop_mode`` lists (``png_size``, ``dialate_pngs``, ``dialate_png_ratios``) are indexed by where the chosen object type sits in ``crop_mode``, and fall back to entry 0 when it is not listed there. The extracted image region's channels come from ``png_channel_mapping`` -- or the legacy ``png_dims`` -- via :func:`channels_from_settings`, so the spec is in colour order, not ``png_dims`` list order. A ``normalize`` that is a sequence of any length but 2 is discarded as ``False``.
records.translation: ``measure_crop`` stillingarnar. Listarnir á hverja ``crop_mode`` (``png_size``, ``dialate_pngs``, ``dialate_png_ratios``) eru skráðir eftir því hvar valinn hlutatýpur situr í ``crop_mode``, og falla til skráar 0 þegar hann er ekki skráður þar. Rásir þeirrar myndar sem er unnin eru fengnar úr ``png_channel_mapping`` -- eða hið eldri ``png_dims`` -- í gegnum :func:`channels_from_settings`, þannig að forskriftin er í litarröð, ekki ``png_dims`` lista röð. ``normalize`` sem er röð af hvaða lengd sem er en ekki 2 er hent sem ``False``.

records.source: **Memoised per frame object.** The classification runs ``Series.nunique()`` over every column, which on a 200 000-row x 48-column measurement table costs 230 ms. Loading one table used to pay that *four* times inside a single ``set_frame`` — this function, plus :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.column_kinds`, plus ``GraphSpec.kinds_for``, plus ``plottable_columns``, each re-deriving the same answer from the same object — 0.9 s of the ~1.9 s the GUI thread spent delivering a freshly loaded frame.
